behaviors.behavior: AC wording is a hard validation: paths, names from the changed code, code-shaped tokens, backticks, ADR/AC/FR numbers are refused; product names, dotted names, end-to-end and a bare slash command pass; every text field is typed
one ask rule: an AC changed or removed, no single owner, or a new area (asked once, approvable); no label ever asks; everything else is decided alone
a restore must name an AC in the base catalog (wording checked); the catalog is read from the base ref, not the working tree
exemption is a claim before the build and refused against an observable diff
answers are bound to run, item index and question wording; no keeps the owner; unattended runs refuse inline and unmarked answers; unattended is read from state, not the flag
CLI: exit codes, escalation names the unit, answer subcommand works from a held result.json, no tracebacks, BOM/UTF-16 text, verify subcommand, UTF-8 output

behaviors.behavior: only a well-formed AC question (non-empty ac_questions, valid sha, attempt id, sub-iterate loop) holds its own unit; every other escalation stops the wave
an unattended question flows from the CLI to a held unit while a second unit of the wave completes

only an operator-signed answer is recorded answered_via operator; a via field or a missing/mismatching signature is self-reported; the answer tool creates the key, signs, and a pick-list letter never exposes an area id
an add may only claim a new id; undeclared edits and freeze differences use the base catalog
--base-ref is required and resolved to the merge-base; a moved base and a stacked unit's own fork point are not inherited
the record is read from the commit, must be append-only and committed no later than the first code
git calls time out, batch reads report missing paths, oversize untracked files are observable, an unreadable spec is an error with its path
the catalog parser reads this repo's shape, the greenfield generator's shape, adopted repos and table-only specs; an unreadable catalog is skipped, never asked or refused
resume path: hold, operator answer, pending, re-claimed under a new attempt, the same question hashes, complete
unchanged is a record kind with its own count bucket and an F11 compare against the diff and a naming test
a no-owner question is a lettered pick list of areas by title in everyday words with a deterministic gloss of at most two jargon terms; picking new area, not-a-promise or a name resolves or explains

the question shows the agent's ORIGINAL promise first and a model's plain wording only as a gloss; a reply that drops, changes or adds a number (whole tokens, number words), negation, limit or quantifier falls back; equivalent spellings pass; an empty area list keeps the plain wording with the deterministic areas

behaviors.behavior: the model is pinned, a ZDR-namespace model is refused, the transport module is loaded once and registered before it runs, and a missing file is a fallback that is never cached
the suggestion cache is one file per key, atomic, re-validated on every hit; a corrupt, foreign or malformed entry is a miss; timeouts and a missing key are never cached

every opt-out fails closed (SHIPWRIGHT_AC_SUGGEST=0, external_review.ac_suggest false, feedback_iterations 0, a gateway, an unreadable config); one 30 s budget per decide call; the model is asked only for a rendered where-does-it-belong question
the decide tool records the suggestion, resumes without asking the model again, and a different campaign nonce does not inherit an old answer

an answer is bound to stable content (id, nonce, item, kind, original promise, options): a moved base still accepts a signed answer without calling the model; a tampered or forged options map is refused or never operator-signed

the signing key is created exclusively (0600), never regenerated, and a bad key file is a clear error; Somewhere new works through a new area; no spec or any unreadable spec is skipped; the F11 unsigned warning is for unattended runs only

[round 8] the question names what the change touches in plain words (Affects, from the changed paths; omitted, never guessed, when a plugin has no plain name), and lists requirements that already use the same key phrase (omitted when none)
[round 8] a change across 2+ plugins, or with no owning area, offers 'applies to several areas' first; picking it mints a cross-cutting requirement recorded on the decision

[round 8] every question asks 'Which requirement would this promise belong to?' and offers 'I do not understand this'; that answer makes the agent reword and the new wording is asked again (exit 11), without calling the model on resume

[round 8] the model's plain wording is shown only when it differs meaningfully from the original; the glossary explains Claude review, outside reviewers and command, and the prompt demands explained jargon
